pspc_ministers.name: Diane Finley
pspc_ministers.role: Minister of Public Works and Government Services
pspc_ministers.notable: Minister when Phoenix Pay implementation received ministerial approval and was advanced. Treasury Board authorities and PWGSC go-forward decisions taken under her portfolio, prior to the 2015 election.

pspc_ministers.name: Judy Foote
pspc_ministers.role: Minister of Public Services and Procurement (first PSPC minister under renamed dept)
pspc_ministers.notable: Phoenix launched under her tenure: Wave 1 on February 24, 2016; Wave 2 on April 21, 2016. Ordered 'pause' of rollout once problems surfaced summer 2016. Resigned from cabinet August 2017 citing family health reasons. Remains the launch-era minister of record.

pspc_ministers.name: Carla Qualtrough
pspc_ministers.role: Minister of Public Services and Procurement
pspc_ministers.notable: Managed the core crisis years 2017-2021. Supervised Goss Gilroy 2018 lessons-learned. Oversaw launch of Next Generation HR and Pay procurement 2018. Responsible minister when AG Ferguson 2018 'incomprehensible failure' report tabled.

pspc_ministers.name: Filomena Tassi
pspc_ministers.role: Minister of Public Services and Procurement
pspc_ministers.notable: Held portfolio during Next Gen HR and Pay scope change (2022 Shared Services realignment) and continuing Phoenix backlog remediation. Tabled Supplementary Estimates for Phoenix stabilization multiple fiscal years.

pspc_ministers.name: Jean-Yves Duclos
pspc_ministers.role: Minister of Public Services and Procurement
pspc_ministers.notable: Took portfolio July 2023. Shepherded PSAC Phoenix damages agreement finalisation and backlog-remediation targets. Former Treasury Board President 2019-2021 - previously on the funding-authority side of Phoenix.

treasury_board_presidents.name: Tony Clement
treasury_board_presidents.notable: Treasury Board President who approved the Phoenix Pay business case, transformation strategy, and funding envelope. Treasury Board secretariat signed off on the IBM-led build and on the parallel decommissioning of the legacy Regional Pay System. Harper-era final authority on the transformation.

treasury_board_presidents.name: Scott Brison
treasury_board_presidents.notable: Treasury Board President covering the 2016 launch and the full crisis emergence. Appeared repeatedly before OGGO committee 2016-2018. Responsible for supplementary estimates approving Phoenix remediation funding. Resigned January 2019.

treasury_board_presidents.name: Mona Fortier
treasury_board_presidents.notable: Treasury Board President during Phoenix stabilization years. Approved Next Generation HR and Pay funding decisions. Negotiating party on PSAC general damages and Phoenix damages agreements.

pspc_deputy_ministers.name: Marie Lemay
pspc_deputy_ministers.role: Deputy Minister of Public Services and Procurement
pspc_deputy_ministers.notable: Deputy Minister PSPC 2016-2020. Operationally responsible senior public servant during Phoenix launch, initial crisis, and remediation planning. Appeared repeatedly before parliamentary committees on Phoenix.

pspc_deputy_ministers.name: Bill Matthews
pspc_deputy_ministers.role: Deputy Minister of Public Services and Procurement
pspc_deputy_ministers.notable: Deputy Minister PSPC 2020-2023. Accountable for Next Generation HR and Pay governance transition and Phoenix backlog-reduction operations. Previously served at TBS on financial management.

auditor_general_oversight.name: Michael Ferguson
auditor_general_oversight.notable: Authored the 2018 Spring Reports Report 1 'Building and Implementing the Phoenix Pay System' and Report 2 'Phoenix Pay Problems'. Landmark finding of an 'incomprehensible failure' of project management and oversight. Died office holder December 2019.

auditor_general_oversight.name: Karen Hogan
auditor_general_oversight.notable: Follow-up Phoenix audits as AG. Continues to flag Phoenix backlog remediation progress in performance audits. Reporting line on the federal pay system remediation outcomes.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Stephen Harper
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: PM when Phoenix business case approved 2009-2011 (IBM contract 2011), parallel Regional Pay System decommissioning planned, and project was accepted into Treasury Board transformation portfolio. Pre-launch PM of record.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Justin Trudeau
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: PM at launch (Feb 2016), through full crisis (2016-2022), AG Ferguson 2018 report, Next Gen procurement, PSAC class action settlements, and damages agreements. Nine-year custody of Phoenix remediation. Cross-axis: Indigenous, RCMP, Veterans, Judicial (quadruple Grover-marked).

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Mark Carney
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: Current PM. Inherits Phoenix remediation commitments, Next Generation HR and Pay delivery timeline, and ongoing backlog reduction targets. Cross-axis: Carney-Brookfield, Indigenous, Veterans, Judicial dossiers.

contract_counterparty.name: IBM Canada (Phoenix prime contractor)
contract_counterparty.role: Prime contractor for Phoenix Pay system build and integration
contract_counterparty.notable: Original 2011 competitive procurement winner. Customised PeopleSoft payroll product for federal HR complexity. 2018 AG report found scope changes and executive decisions reduced the build from the planned full scope; project-management failure attributed to both Crown and contractor sides. Contract value exceeded $300M and Phoenix total federal costs have exceeded $2.4B.

timeline.event: Transformation of Pay Administration Initiative launched under Harper government.
IBM Canada selected as prime contractor for Phoenix Pay build.
Phoenix Pay business case and Treasury Board approvals advanced.
Phoenix Wave 1 launch: 34 federal departments onboarded.
Phoenix Wave 2 launch: remaining 67 departments onboarded; pay errors begin scaling.
Minister Foote acknowledges widespread pay problems; backlog reported >80,000 cases.
AG Ferguson reports Phoenix oversight concerns in Spring 2017 report.
AG Ferguson tables 'Building and Implementing the Phoenix Pay System': 'incomprehensible failure'. Senate report echoes findings.
Goss Gilroy Phoenix Lessons Learned report commissioned.
Next Generation HR and Pay procurement launched.
Goss Gilroy Phoenix Lessons Learned report published.
PSAC Phoenix damages general agreement signed - up to $2,500 per employee.
Phoenix backlog remains >100,000 open transactions; Next Gen scope revised.
Phoenix supplementary damages agreement / PSAC Bouchard class action settlement advanced.
AG Hogan follow-up on federal pay system - continuing remediation gaps.
Carney government inherits Phoenix remediation + Next Gen delivery commitments.

accountability_chain.result_2025: Phoenix Pay remains in operation under stabilisation. Total federal costs exceed $2.4B. Backlog reduced from peak but not zero. Next Generation HR and Pay procurement ongoing under SSC. PSAC Phoenix damages agreement + supplementary class action settlements have compensated federal workers. No ministerial or senior-official criminal liability. No contract-recoupment from IBM.
